thread:
incident-bot: Paging oncall -> API Gateway edge: elevated 502/504 spike detected (16:11 UTC). Error rate 70% on /v1/generate in us-west-2, auto-threshold breached. Paging @oncall_api

Aisha: seeing the page, oncall?

Kai: I'm on it, pulling edge metrics and upstream traces now

Aisha: quick triage ask — is this gateway-level or app-level? any 5xx from model pool?

Kai: initial look: 502s are coming from gateway returning upstream timeout / bad-gateway. App logs show upstream timeouts to model-pool-primary nodes.

Maria: dashboards show backend latencies spiking right before 502s, but CPU/mem look normal on the model nodes. Connection errors + read timeouts.

Sahil: tried a manual curl against gateway in us-west-2 -> get 502 and a short body: "upstream read timeout"

oncall_api: Assigned -> Kai (oncall_api)

Kai: I'm going to put a quick traffic fallback to model-pool-legacy and enable a conservative circuit-breaker for the generate route.

Aisha: good. Also need customer-impact estimate and whether to post a status page. Jon, you're PM on SLOs — thoughts?

Jon: If error-rate stays >1% for more than 5m we need a status page inbound. Right now cluster-wide spike at 70% in a region — likely customer visible. Please prepare a short message.

Kai: applying route change now. Patch snippet:
```
route "generate" {
  max_concurrency = 8
  fallback = ["model-pool-legacy"]
  failure_threshold = 0.15
}
```

Maria: CB applied. Error-rate dropped from 72% -> 48% within 30s. Still elevated but improving.

Sahil: autoscale shows primary pool at nominal capacity; no instant headroom to scale further. Requesting a manual scale on legacy pool.

Aisha: go ahead, provision +4 nodes to legacy pool as hotfix. Ops, please kick it.

ops-bot: Provision request accepted: legacy-pool +4 nodes. ETA ~90s (req 98765).

Kai: while that provisions, I'm checking kernel and socket metrics on model-pool-primary. Seeing a burst of FD usage and some kernel-level connection drops (RST).

Maria: logs: multiple upstream TCP RST entries around 16:11:58 UTC for model-pool-primary on 443. Not seeing OOMs though.

Sahil: that points to connection exhaustion or ephemeral port exhaustion on proxy -> backend. Increasing fd limits and restarting proxy agents on affected pool nodes.

Kai: increasing ulimit/fd and restarting proxy agent on 4 nodes now. Commands run:
```
sudo sysctl -w fs.file-max=200000
ulimit -n 65536
systemctl restart redwood-proxy
```

ops-bot: restart completed on 4 nodes (req 98766).

Maria: after restart, socket errors drop and backend reports fewer RSTs. Error-rate trending down to ~12% in us-west-2.

Sahil: legacy pool scaled, traffic shifted to legacy fallback. End-to-end 502s now ~6% overall across all regions.

Aisha: customer impact assessment: partial degradation affecting ~1.1% of global requests; concentrated in high-volume PLG cohorts and a handful of paid accounts in us-west. Recommend status page and targeted CS outreach.

support-bot: Created CS outreach ticket CS-592 for affected accounts (attached request ids).

Jon: okay, publish status page with minimal detail (investigating gateway errors, mitigation in progress). I'll draft.

Kai: collecting sample request_ids for the failed 502s and grabbing full proxy traces for RCA. Query used:
```
index=proxy_logs status=502 path=/v1/generate | limit 200
```

Maria: trace logs show client connections were fine; proxy had diminished available fds and triggered connection errors to upstream pool. Kernel dropped connections first, not app process level.

Sahil: looks like root cause = ephemeral fd exhaustion on proxy agents + aggressive concurrency from PLG workloads. Triggered cascade when upstream briefly misbehaved.

Aisha: mitigation summary: 1) fallback route to legacy, 2) circuit-breaker on generate, 3) increased fd limits + proxy agent restarts, 4) manual scale of legacy pool. Error-rate now <=5% and stable for 3m.

Kai: marking mitigation stable. Will keep fallback + CB for observation window (30m). After stable window, revert fallback and gradually relax CB.

Maria: FYI I opened NET ticket for short DNS flapping seen on edge proxies right before the spike. net-bot created NET-338.

net-bot: NET-338 created: investigate edge DNS and LB health checks (assigned to Net Infra).

Aisha: immediate next steps: notify CS + publish status page (Jon), collect logs for RCA (Kai/Maria), schedule postmortem (Aisha), adjust autoscaling / concurrency defaults (follow-up).

Jon: I'll publish the status update and coordinate with communications.

Aisha: handing off ongoing monitoring to night oncall. oncall_api_night, you're up to watch for the next 4 hours.

oncall_api_night: ack. I will keep an eye, will escalate if errors climb >3% again.

Kai: one more note — pulling perf profile for proxy agent to see if fd leak is application-level.

Maria: saved diagnostic bundles to ops/incidents/2864123456/diagnostics.tar.gz

Aisha: assigning RCA owners: Aisha (incident lead) and Kai (runtime/proxy deep dive). We'll include NET-338 in scope.

Kai: thumbs up :thumbsup:

Aisha: closing live triage thread. We'll reopen if any regression. Final action: keep CB + fallback for 30m, then start staged revert. Postmortem owner: Aisha, target draft in 48h.

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity: Sev2. Tags: api-gateway, 502, fd-exhaustion, fallback-applied.
